lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 6 years old and lives here at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have a son, Alex, who is 6 years old and lives with you at home.

Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Birmingham.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. That's helpful information.

Now I need to ask:

**Are you responsible for Alex's day-to-day care? For example, do you provide for his food, clothes, and other needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I look after him every day - I make sure he's fed, clothed, and take care of everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. 

Let me ask a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you.

Just a few more questions:

**Is Alex currently in any of the following situations:**
- In hospital or residential accommodation for an extended period?
- In local authority care?
- Living with someone else (not with you)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply. He lives here with me full-time and isn't in hospital or care or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for clarifying that.

One final question:

**Do you have the right to reside in the UK? For example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or another immigration status that gives you the right to live here?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a UK citizen, so I have the right to live here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the requirements for Child Benefit:

✓ Alex is 6 years old (under 16)
✓ You live in the UK (Birmingham)
✓ You are responsible for Alex's day-to-day care
✓ Alex lives with you full-time
✓ You're a UK citizen with the right to reside in the UK
✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
✓ Alex is not in hospital, care, or living elsewhere

**Next steps:**
You can now proceed to make a claim for Child Benefit. You'll need to apply through HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC).

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might have to pay some or all of it back through your tax return.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
